circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for Formula One's season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street course encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne that hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year, alongside the Supercars Championship and various support events. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 racing licence.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km motorsport venue that has twice hosted the Austrian Grand Prix, first during an 18-year period from 1970 to 1987 under its original name Österreichring, and again from 1997 to 2003 following its renovation and renaming as the A1-Ring.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, measuring 6. 003 km and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix and continues to stage the annual F1 race alongside other motorsport events including GP2 racing and 24-hour endurance competitions. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and features multiple circuit configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a diverse layout combining extended straights with varied cornering sections, making it a versatile test of driver and machine capabilities. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its stands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa is a 7. 004 km Belgian racing circuit situated near the town of Spa in Wallonia, renowned for hosting the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix. The venue has participated in F1 racing since 1950, the championship's inaugural season, and has maintained consistent annual Grand Prix events from 1985 onwards with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the home of the FIA Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport series including sportscar championships and North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the country's Formula One grand prix annually between 2004 and 2019, before resuming the event from 2024 onward. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing competitions alongside its primary Formula One championship rounds.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Northamptonshire in England, Silverstone Circuit has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After sharing hosting duties with other British venues from 1955 to 1986, the Grand Prix became permanently based at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, while the track also stages MotoGP racing events.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit located near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it debuted in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue at the time, the track was constructed outside the capital after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's largest park were rejected by the government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility. It has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, except during 1980 when it underwent renovation, and earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" from its characteristically long straightaways and quick-corner design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport facility operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, hosting up to 155,000 spectators. The track primarily serves as a venue for Formula One and Japanese Super Formula racing championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, utilizing roads adjacent to the famous Las Vegas Strip along Las Vegas Boulevard. The layout weaves past iconic venues including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, which line the thoroughfare known for its major hotels and casinos.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two deceased racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who both died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in multiple eras, returning to the calendar in 2015 with its current layout after a 23-year absence.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary racing circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that debuted on the Formula One calendar in 2022. Spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners, the track was specially designed by Apex Circuit Design and produces average qualifying speeds near 139 mph.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, encircling the harbor of the principality. The track is typically known as Monte Carlo because the majority of its layout occupies the Monte Carlo area.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km circuit that reclaimed its place on the Formula One schedule in 2021 with the restoration of the Dutch Grand Prix. The venue will host the championship for five seasons before concluding its F1 partnership in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari motor racing venue situated north of Doha near the city of Lusail. The 5. 419 km track features a 1.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian motorsport facility in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aviation accident eight years prior. The counterclockwise track hosts the Brazilian Grand Prix and features a karting circuit dedicated to fellow racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: Situated along Jeddah's waterfront on the Red Sea, the Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street-based racing venue that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021 and began accommodating Formula E racing in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a temporary road course laid out around Singapore's Marina Bay, incorporating portions of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657-kilometre facility features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner types that test multiple aspects of vehicle performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Situated in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the venue for Formula One's United States Grand Prix alongside major motorsports events including MotoGP and endurance racing competitions. The track has historically accommodated numerous racing series, ranging from NASCAR to IndyCar events.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who currently races for Williams, competing under Thailand's flag in Formula One.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having claimed two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 alongside 32 Grand Prix victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved considerable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories with Toyota and the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both the Formula One drivers' title and the World Endurance equivalent.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined the Mercedes Formula One team starting in 2025 and has secured six Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who currently races for Haas in Formula One.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian motorsport competitor, currently races in Formula One as a driver for Audi.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing experience from a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, and has recorded 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his tenure in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One for the Alpine team. He represents his country in the sport's premier motorsport championship.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian driver who holds a reserve role at Haas in Formula One while competing in European endurance racing. He made seven Grand Prix appearances between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French driver currently competing in Formula One for Alpine, previously achieved a significant victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Hadjar is a French-Algerian motorsport competitor who represents France in Formula One, currently racing for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton, a British driver competing for Ferrari, has achieved seven World Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple Formula One records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved endurance racing success by winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver Charles Leclerc has been competing for Ferrari in Formula One, where he finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship. Throughout his nine seasons in the sport, he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024, before transitioning to other racing disciplines. He currently competes as a factory driver for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT, while also undertaking part-time NASCAR commitments with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship title with the team. Throughout his eight-season career, he has achieved 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Haas. Earlier in his career, he achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez represents Mexico on the Formula One grid, currently driving for Cadillac. The veteran competitor finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his 15-season career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, currently races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his time competing across four seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One over a 14-year span from 2011 through 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," he was a prominent figure in the sport across more than a decade of competition.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories over his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes in Formula One for Williams and has secured four Grand Prix victories during his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following previous stints in IMSA's LMP2 class. He had a brief Formula One career spanning 2023 and 2024.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor who currently drives for Aston Martin in Formula One racing.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, has held reserve positions with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls throughout his Formula One career spanning from 2021 to 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: A Dutch and Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Verstappen has secured four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles from 2021 through 2024. His career achievements include 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated over 12 seasons in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the sport from 2022 to 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, inheriting Renault's works team status following a rebranding of what was previously the Renault F1 Team. Operating under French licensing and powered by Mercedes engines, Alpine secured its only victory during this era through Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix before Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained an intermittent presence in Formula One racing across multiple team formats, with its current incarnation operating under the AMR GP Limited structure.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, Italy's legendary racing outfit, has participated in every Formula One World Championship since the sport's inaugural 1950 season, making it both the oldest continuously competing team and the most accomplished in the sport's history. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" for its iconic emblem, the team represents Ferrari's racing heritage and continues as a cornerstone competitor in modern Formula One.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American Formula One outfit founded by Gene Haas and entering the sport in 2016, the team competes under an American license in the championship. Leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had overseen operations since the team's establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Sauber was a Swiss motorsport engineering firm established in 1970 that achieved prominence in endurance racing, including a Le Mans victory in 1989, before competing in Formula One from 1993 until 2025. Operating as an independent constructor for much of its history, the team became the fourth-longest-running chassis supplier in the sport before Audi acquired its operations and infrastructure in 2024 to establish its own F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited operates as a British Formula One competitor based at its technology headquarters in Woking. The team functions as part of the McLaren Group, which is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current team operating from Brackley under a German license. The squad, known colloquially as the "Silver Arrows," became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and Toto Wolff starting in January 2022. The team competes under the Mercedes-AMG Petronas banner in the modern championship era.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as part of Red Bull's multi-team strategy. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates alongside Red Bull Racing under the Austrian conglomerate's ownership structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that debuted in 2024 as the second team owned by Red Bull GmbH, complementing Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operational support from Milton Keynes, the outfit operates as a sister team within Red Bull's two-team Formula One structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team established in 2005 and headquartered in England, operating as one of two racing entities owned by the Red Bull conglomerate. Under Christian Horner's two-decade tenure as team principal, the squad became a dominant force in the sport, though Mekies assumed leadership in 2025 following Horner's departure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor founded by Frank Williams and Patrick Head in 1977, evolved from Williams's previous unsuccessful racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team banner and operates from a substantial 60-acre facility.
